R/huff.R 
# =============================================================================
# R/huff.R -- the probabilistic spatial interaction model, in matrix form
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# For origin i and station j,
#
#   P_ij = A_j f(d_ij) / (A_0 + sum_k A_k f(d_ik)),   E_j = sum_i M_i P_ij
#
# with attractiveness A_j = exp(x_j' beta + r_j), distance decay f, and a local
# market M_i that is a weighted sum of one or more market columns. A_0 is an optional
# outside option, the choice of not using the rail network at all; with A_0 = 0 this
# is the Huff model. MCI::huff.shares() computes the same shares, as 05_calibrate.R
# confirms, but it works through a data frame and cannot be called thousands of
# times inside a calibration, so the calibration uses these matrix forms.
# =============================================================================

decay_g <- function(D, type = c("pow", "exp")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  if (type == "pow") log(D) else D
}

# lA: log attractiveness (length J); lf: log decay (I x J). Everything stays on the
# log scale, because A_j f(d_ij) spans many orders of magnitude across the island.
huff_prob <- function(lA, lf, lA0 = NULL) {
  u  <- sweep(lf, 2, lA, "+")
  mx <- apply(u, 1, max)
  if (!is.null(lA0)) mx <- pmax(mx, lA0)
  # A hexagon with no station inside the maximum access distance sends no one.
  mx[!is.finite(mx)] <- 0
  v  <- exp(u - mx)
  den <- rowSums(v)
  if (!is.null(lA0)) den <- den + exp(lA0 - mx)
  den[den == 0] <- 1
  v / den
}

# par = (lambda, beta..., log kappa..., [log A0])
unpack <- function(par, spec) {
  p <- ncol(spec$X); m <- ncol(spec$M)
  list(lambda = par[1],
       beta   = if (p > 0) par[1 + seq_len(p)] else numeric(0),
       kappa  = exp(par[1 + p + seq_len(m)]),
       lA0    = if (isTRUE(spec$use_A0)) par[2 + p + m] else NULL)
}

model_parts <- function(par, spec, D = spec$D, X = spec$X, M = spec$M, r = NULL) {
  q  <- unpack(par, spec)
  lA <- if (ncol(X) > 0) as.vector(X %*% q$beta) else rep(0, ncol(D))
  if (!is.null(r)) lA <- lA + r
  g  <- decay_g(D, spec$type)
  lf <- q$lambda * g
  # The choice set stops at a maximum access distance, because no one reaches their
  # boarding station from 20 km away, however small the probability a decay gives it.
  if (!is.null(spec$dmax)) lf[D > spec$dmax] <- -Inf
  P  <- huff_prob(lA, lf, q$lA0)
  mk <- as.vector(M %*% q$kappa)
  list(q = q, lA = lA, g = g, P = P, mk = mk, E = as.vector(crossprod(mk, P)))
}

expected <- function(par, spec, ...) model_parts(par, spec, ...)$E

# Squared error on the log scale. Ridership runs from under 200 to over 70,000 a day,
# and the stations this exercise cares about most are at the bottom of that range; on
# the raw scale the fit would be decided by a dozen interchanges.
loss <- function(par, spec) {
  E <- expected(par, spec)
  w <- if (is.null(spec$w)) 1 else spec$w
  sum(w * (log(spec$T) - log(pmax(E, 1e-6)))^2)
}

# Exact gradient of the loss. The validation and bootstrap run hundreds of
# calibrations, so finite differences, at one model run per parameter, are avoided.
grad_loss <- function(par, spec) {
  z <- model_parts(par, spec)
  P <- z$P; g <- z$g; mk <- z$mk; E <- pmax(z$E, 1e-6)
  w <- -2 * (if (is.null(spec$w)) 1 else spec$w) * (log(spec$T) - log(E)) / E
  gbar <- rowSums(P * g)
  out <- sum(w * (colSums(mk * P * g) - as.vector(crossprod(mk * gbar, P))))
  X <- spec$X
  if (ncol(X) > 0) {
    xbar <- P %*% X
    cs <- colSums(mk * P)
    out <- c(out, vapply(seq_len(ncol(X)), function(m) {
      sum(w * (X[, m] * cs - as.vector(crossprod(mk * xbar[, m], P))))
    }, numeric(1)))
  }
  out <- c(out, vapply(seq_len(ncol(spec$M)), function(m) {
    sum(w * z$q$kappa[m] * as.vector(crossprod(spec$M[, m], P)))
  }, numeric(1)))
  if (isTRUE(spec$use_A0)) {
    P0 <- 1 - rowSums(P)
    out <- c(out, sum(w * (-as.vector(crossprod(mk * P0, P)))))
  }
  out
}

start_par <- function(spec, lambda0) {
  c(lambda0, rep(0, ncol(spec$X)), rep(-1, ncol(spec$M)),
    if (isTRUE(spec$use_A0)) -2)
}

fit_huff <- function(spec, lambda0 = if (spec$type == "pow") -1.5 else -0.3,
                     par0 = NULL, maxit = 300, fix_lambda = NULL) {
  if (is.null(par0)) par0 <- start_par(spec, lambda0)
  if (!is.null(fix_lambda)) {
    # Holds lambda at a given value, for the profile and for the literature's -2.
    fn <- function(th) loss(c(fix_lambda, th), spec)
    gr <- function(th) grad_loss(c(fix_lambda, th), spec)[-1]
    fit <- optim(par0[-1], fn, gr, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = maxit, reltol = 1e-8))
    fit$par <- c(fix_lambda, fit$par)
  } else {
    fit <- optim(par0, loss, grad_loss, spec = spec, method = "BFGS",
                 control = list(maxit = maxit, reltol = 1e-8))
  }
  fit$E <- expected(fit$par, spec)
  fit$spec <- spec
  fit
}

fit_stats <- function(T, E) {
  e <- log(T) - log(E)
  tibble::tibble(rmsle = sqrt(mean(e^2)),
                 r2_log = 1 - sum(e^2) / sum((log(T) - mean(log(T)))^2),
                 mape = median(abs(E / T - 1)),
                 rho = cor(T, E, method = "spearman"))
}

# Station-specific attractiveness that reproduces observed ridership exactly, given
# lambda and the market. The multiplicative update is the one huff.fit() in MCI
# applies; here it runs on the whole matrix at once. A closed model allocates all of
# its market, so its total must equal total ridership before the update can converge;
# a log-scale fit leaves it a little short, so the market is rescaled first. Without
# an outside option r is defined only up to a constant, which is fixed by giving r a
# mean of zero, so that r = 0 is what a typical station has and a new station is
# given. `r0` allows a warm start.
closure_par <- function(par, spec) {
  if (isTRUE(spec$use_A0)) return(par)
  mk <- as.vector(spec$M %*% unpack(par, spec)$kappa)
  p <- ncol(spec$X); m <- ncol(spec$M)
  par[1 + p + seq_len(m)] <- par[1 + p + seq_len(m)] + log(sum(spec$T) / sum(mk))
  par
}

calibrate_r <- function(par, spec, r0 = NULL, tol = 1e-4, maxit = 3000) {
  par <- closure_par(par, spec)
  r <- if (is.null(r0)) rep(0, ncol(spec$D)) else r0
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    E <- expected(par, spec, r = r)
    ratio <- spec$T / pmax(E, 1e-9)
    gap <- max(abs(ratio - 1))
    if (gap < tol) break
    r <- r + log(ratio)
  }
  if (!isTRUE(spec$use_A0)) r <- r - mean(r)
  list(par = par, r = r, iterations = it, max_gap = gap)
}
R/rail.R 
# =============================================================================
# R/rail.R -- the rail network as a graph
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# Lines are written out as ordered station codes. Station-to-station times are distance
# over a running speed that includes stops, and changing lines costs a fixed penalty.
# These are assumptions rather than measurements. Each station has separate entry and
# exit nodes, so that a path can only change lines by paying the transfer penalty, and
# never by passing through a station's gates.
# =============================================================================

SPEED <- c(MRT = 35, LRT = 20, JRL = 30)   # km/h, including dwell
TRANSFER_MIN <- 5

seqn <- function(p, v) paste0(p, v)
NETWORK <- list(
  NS = list(seqn("NS", c(1:5, 7:28)), "MRT"),
  EW = list(seqn("EW", 1:33), "MRT"),
  CG = list(c("EW4", "CG1", "CG2"), "MRT"),
  NE = list(seqn("NE", c(1, 3:18)), "MRT"),
  CC = list(c(seqn("CC", c(1:17, 19:32)), "CE2", "CE1", "CC4"), "MRT"),
  DT = list(seqn("DT", 1:35), "MRT"),
  TE = list(seqn("TE", c(1:9, 11:20, 22:29)), "MRT"),
  BP = list(c(seqn("BP", 1:13), "BP6"), "LRT"),
  SE = list(c("STC", seqn("SE", 1:5), "STC"), "LRT"),
  SW = list(c("STC", seqn("SW", 1:8), "STC"), "LRT"),
  PE = list(c("PTC", seqn("PE", 1:7), "PTC"), "LRT"),
  PW = list(c("PTC", seqn("PW", 1:7), "PTC"), "LRT")
)
# The Jurong Region Line's three arms meet at Tengah and Bahar Junction. Its medium
# capacity trains are given a lower speed than heavy rail.
PROPOSED <- list(
  JS = list(seqn("JS", 1:12), "JRL"),
  JW = list(c("JS7", seqn("JW", 1:5)), "JRL"),
  JE = list(c("JS3", seqn("JE", 1:7)), "JRL"),
  CR = list(seqn("CR", 2:13), "MRT")
)

# cx: one row per code with station_id, x, y
build_graph <- function(lines, cx, transfer = TRANSFER_MIN) {
  link <- purrr::map_dfr(names(lines), function(nm) {
    s <- lines[[nm]][[1]]
    tibble::tibble(from = s[-length(s)], to = s[-1], line = nm, mode = lines[[nm]][[2]])
  })
  link <- link |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cx, code, fx = x, fy = y), by = c("from" = "code")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cx, code, tx = x, ty = y), by = c("to" = "code")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(km = sqrt((fx - tx)^2 + (fy - ty)^2) / 1000,
                  minutes = km / SPEED[mode] * 60, type = "ride") |>
    dplyr::select(from, to, line, minutes, km, type)
  used_st <- dplyr::filter(cx, code %in% unique(c(link$from, link$to)))
  gates <- used_st |>
    dplyr::transmute(from = paste0("IN_", station_id), to = code, line = NA_character_,
                     minutes = 0, km = 0, type = "enter")
  exits <- used_st |>
    dplyr::transmute(from = code, to = paste0("OUT_", station_id), line = NA_character_,
                     minutes = 0, km = 0, type = "exit")
  xfer <- used_st |>
    dplyr::inner_join(used_st, by = "station_id", suffix = c("_a", "_b"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    dplyr::filter(code_a != code_b) |>
    dplyr::transmute(from = code_a, to = code_b, line = NA_character_, minutes = transfer,
                     km = 0, type = "transfer")
  rides <- dplyr::bind_rows(link, dplyr::rename(link, from = to, to = from))
  igraph::graph_from_data_frame(dplyr::bind_rows(rides, gates, exits, xfer), directed = TRUE)
}

rail_matrix <- function(g, ids) {
  m <- igraph::distances(g, v = paste0("IN_", ids), to = paste0("OUT_", ids), mode = "out",
                         weights = igraph::E(g)$minutes)
  dimnames(m) <- list(ids, ids)
  m
}
scripts/01_markets.R 
# =============================================================================
# 01_markets.R -- origin markets: where the potential MRT users live
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# Builds the local market potential that the spatial interaction model allocates
# to stations. HDB's building layer has footprints but no dwelling counts, and
# its property table has dwelling counts but no geometry and no shared street
# field, so the two are first linked through a crosswalk recovered from the data.
# Subzone residents are then spread onto HDB blocks by flat type and onto private
# housing through OpenStreetMap buildings, and summed to a hexagon grid.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex3/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(stringr)
})
sf_use_s2(FALSE)   # planar operations: everything is moved to SVY21 first

RAW <- "data/raw"; DER <- "data/derived"
dir.create(DER, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
SVY21 <- 3414
HEX_M <- 500       # flat-to-flat width of the origin hexagons, in metres
audit <- list()

# ---- Subzones ---------------------------------------------------------------
# The Master Plan 2019 layer has six invalid polygons and a Z dimension. Both
# would break the spatial joins below, so they are repaired on import.
sz <- st_read(file.path(RAW, "boundary/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSea.geojson"),
              quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_zm()
audit$sz_invalid <- sum(!st_is_valid(sz))
sz <- sz |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(SVY21) |>
  transmute(SZ = SUBZONE_N, PA = PLN_AREA_N, REGION = REGION_N)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sz$SZ))
land <- st_union(sz)

# ---- HDB: the street crosswalk ----------------------------------------------
# The building layer identifies a street by a code (YIR00Z) and the property
# table by a name (YISHUN RING RD). No published table links them, but both list
# the same block numbers, so a street code and a street name that share the same
# set of blocks are the same street. Block numbers repeat across the island, so
# overlap alone can tie (KG KAYU RD, SAGO LANE); the code's letters, which
# abbreviate the street, break those ties.
bld <- st_read(file.path(RAW, "hdb/HDBExistingBuilding.geojson"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_zm()
audit$bld_n       <- nrow(bld)
audit$bld_invalid <- sum(!st_is_valid(bld))
bld <- bld |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(SVY21) |>
  transmute(blk = toupper(trimws(BLK_NO)), ST_COD, POSTAL_COD)

prop <- read_csv(file.path(RAW, "hdb/HDBPropertyInformation.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(blk = toupper(trimws(blk_no)))
audit$prop_n <- nrow(prop)
audit$prop_du <- sum(prop$total_dwelling_units)

n_cod <- count(st_drop_geometry(bld), ST_COD, name = "n_cod")
n_str <- count(prop, street, name = "n_str")

prefix_score <- function(code, street) {
  pre   <- substr(code, 1, 3)
  words <- strsplit(gsub("[^A-Z0-9 ]", "", street), " ")[[1]]
  best  <- 0
  for (w in words) for (k in 3:1) {
    if (substr(w, 1, k) == substr(pre, 1, k)) { best <- max(best, k); break }
  }
  best / 3
}

pairs <- st_drop_geometry(bld) |>
  select(blk, ST_COD) |>
  inner_join(select(prop, blk, street), by = "blk", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(ST_COD, street, name = "n_common") |>
  left_join(n_cod, by = "ST_COD") |>
  left_join(n_str, by = "street") |>
  mutate(jaccard = n_common / (n_cod + n_str - n_common),
         letters = mapply(prefix_score, ST_COD, street),
         score   = jaccard + 0.5 * letters) |>
  arrange(desc(score), desc(n_common))

# Greedy one-to-one assignment, best pair first.
take <- logical(nrow(pairs)); seen_c <- character(); seen_s <- character()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
  if (!pairs$ST_COD[i] %in% seen_c && !pairs$street[i] %in% seen_s) {
    take[i] <- TRUE
    seen_c  <- c(seen_c, pairs$ST_COD[i]); seen_s <- c(seen_s, pairs$street[i])
  }
}
crosswalk <- pairs[take, ]
audit$cw_codes    <- nrow(n_cod)
audit$cw_streets  <- nrow(n_str)
audit$cw_assigned <- nrow(crosswalk)
audit$cw_perfect  <- sum(crosswalk$jaccard == 1)
audit$cw_unassigned_codes   <- setdiff(n_cod$ST_COD, crosswalk$ST_COD)
audit$cw_unassigned_streets <- setdiff(n_str$street, crosswalk$street)

bld_pts <- bld |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  left_join(select(crosswalk, ST_COD, street), by = "ST_COD")

blocks <- prop |>
  filter(residential == "Y") |>
  left_join(select(bld_pts, blk, street, geometry), by = c("blk", "street")) |>
  mutate(has_footprint = !st_is_empty(st_sfc(geometry, crs = SVY21)))

audit$bld_matched     <- sum(paste(bld_pts$blk, bld_pts$street) %in%
                               paste(prop$blk, prop$street))
audit$res_blocks      <- nrow(blocks)
audit$res_du          <- sum(blocks$total_dwelling_units)
audit$res_no_footprint    <- sum(!blocks$has_footprint)
audit$res_no_footprint_du <- sum(blocks$total_dwelling_units[!blocks$has_footprint])
audit$res_no_footprint_years <- sort(unique(blocks$year_completed[!blocks$has_footprint]))

# Blocks completed after the footprint layer was last revised have no geometry.
# Each is placed at the centre of the other blocks on its street, or left for the
# geocoded list below when the whole street is new.
street_centre <- blocks |>
  filter(has_footprint) |>
  st_as_sf(crs = SVY21) |>
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(street) |>
  summarise(sx = mean(x), sy = mean(y), .groups = "drop")

xy <- st_coordinates(st_as_sf(filter(blocks, has_footprint), crs = SVY21))
blocks$x <- NA_real_; blocks$y <- NA_real_
blocks$x[blocks$has_footprint] <- xy[, 1]
blocks$y[blocks$has_footprint] <- xy[, 2]
blocks <- blocks |>
  select(-geometry) |>
  left_join(street_centre, by = "street") |>
  mutate(placed = case_when(has_footprint ~ "footprint",
                            !is.na(sx) ~ "street centre",
                            TRUE ~ "none"),
         x = coalesce(x, sx), y = coalesce(y, sy)) |>
  select(-sx, -sy)
audit$res_placed <- count(blocks, placed, wt = total_dwelling_units)
unplaced <- filter(blocks, placed == "none")
audit$res_unplaced <- unplaced |> select(blk, street, year_completed, total_dwelling_units)
blocks <- filter(blocks, placed != "none")

# Flat types, grouped to match the dwelling categories of the population table.
blocks <- blocks |>
  mutate(g12 = `1room_sold` + `2room_sold` + studio_apartment_sold + `1room_rental` +
               `2room_rental` + other_room_rental,
         g3  = `3room_sold` + `3room_rental`,
         g4  = `4room_sold`,
         g5  = `5room_sold` + exec_sold + multigen_sold) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = SVY21) |>
  st_join(select(sz, SZ, PA), join = st_nearest_feature)

# ---- Residents by subzone ---------------------------------------------------
pop <- read_csv(file.path(RAW, "popn/respopagesextod2024.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(SZ = toupper(SZ)) |>
  group_by(SZ, TOD) |>
  summarise(Pop = sum(Pop), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(group = case_when(
    TOD == "HDB 1- and 2-Room Flats" ~ "g12",
    TOD == "HDB 3-Room Flats" ~ "g3",
    TOD == "HDB 4-Room Flats" ~ "g4",
    TOD %in% c("HDB 5-Room and Executive Flats",
               "HUDC Flats (excluding those privatised)") ~ "g5",
    TOD == "Condominiums and Other Apartments" ~ "condo",
    TOD == "Landed Properties" ~ "landed",
    TRUE ~ "other")) |>
  group_by(SZ, group) |>
  summarise(Pop = sum(Pop), .groups = "drop")

audit$pop_total <- sum(pop$Pop)
audit$pop_by_group <- pop |> group_by(group) |> summarise(Pop = sum(Pop), .groups = "drop")
audit$pop_sz_unmatched <- setdiff(unique(pop$SZ[pop$Pop > 0]), sz$SZ)

# ---- Residents onto HDB blocks ----------------------------------------------
# Persons per flat are computed within each subzone and flat type, from blocks
# standing at the population reference date (June 2024). Blocks completed since
# then are not in that count, so they receive the island-wide persons per flat of
# their type instead: the ridership being modelled is from 2026, when they are
# occupied. Blocks completed during 2026 are left out of the base market because
# their keys are still being collected, and kept for the 2030 scenario.
REF_YEAR <- 2024
GROUPS <- c("g12", "g3", "g4", "g5")

long <- blocks |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(blk, street, SZ, year_completed, all_of(GROUPS)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(GROUPS), names_to = "group", values_to = "flats") |>
  filter(flats > 0)

stand <- long |>
  filter(year_completed <= REF_YEAR) |>
  group_by(SZ, group) |>
  summarise(flats_sz = sum(flats), .groups = "drop")

ppf_sz <- pop |>
  filter(group %in% GROUPS) |>
  full_join(stand, by = c("SZ", "group")) |>
  mutate(Pop = coalesce(Pop, 0), flats_sz = coalesce(flats_sz, 0),
         ppf = ifelse(flats_sz > 0, Pop / flats_sz, NA_real_))

ppf_city <- ppf_sz |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(ppf_city = sum(Pop[flats_sz > 0]) / sum(flats_sz), .groups = "drop")
audit$ppf_city <- ppf_city

# Residents recorded in a flat type a subzone does not have: the two sources
# disagree slightly because HUDC estates and en-bloc sites are classified
# differently. These are spread over the subzone's other blocks.
orphans <- ppf_sz |> filter(flats_sz == 0, Pop > 0)
audit$pop_orphan_hdb <- sum(orphans$Pop)

long <- long |>
  left_join(select(ppf_sz, SZ, group, ppf), by = c("SZ", "group")) |>
  left_join(ppf_city, by = "group") |>
  mutate(is_new = year_completed > REF_YEAR,
         res = flats * ifelse(is_new | is.na(ppf), ppf_city, ppf))

orphan_sz <- orphans |> group_by(SZ) |> summarise(orphan = sum(Pop), .groups = "drop")
block_res <- long |>
  group_by(blk, street, SZ) |>
  summarise(res = sum(res), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(orphan_sz, by = "SZ") |>
  group_by(SZ) |>
  mutate(res = res + coalesce(orphan, 0) * res / sum(res)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-orphan)

blocks <- blocks |>
  left_join(select(block_res, blk, street, res), by = c("blk", "street")) |>
  mutate(res = coalesce(res, 0))
audit$hdb_res_base <- sum(blocks$res[blocks$year_completed <= 2025])
audit$hdb_res_2026 <- sum(blocks$res[blocks$year_completed == 2026])
audit$hdb_du_2026  <- sum(blocks$total_dwelling_units[blocks$year_completed == 2026])
audit$hdb_du_new_since_ref <- sum(blocks$total_dwelling_units[blocks$year_completed > REF_YEAR &
                                                                blocks$year_completed <= 2025])

# ---- Residents in private housing -------------------------------------------
# Nearly a quarter of residents live outside HDB estates, and no official layer
# locates them. Condominium residents are placed on OpenStreetMap apartment and residential
# buildings by footprint area, and landed residents on house-type buildings by
# count, within each subzone. Buildings on an HDB footprint are removed first,
# because OSM tags HDB blocks as residential too.
Z <- paste0("/vsizip/", RAW, "/osm/malaysia-singapore-brunei-latest-free.shp.zip/")
bb <- st_as_text(st_as_sfc(st_bbox(st_transform(sz, 4326))))
osm_b <- st_read(paste0(Z, "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.shp"), wkt_filter = bb, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(SVY21) |>
  select(type)
osm_b$area <- as.numeric(st_area(osm_b))
osm_pts <- st_point_on_surface(osm_b)
osm_pts <- st_filter(osm_pts, land)
audit$osm_b_n <- nrow(osm_pts)

on_hdb <- lengths(st_intersects(osm_pts, bld)) > 0
audit$osm_b_on_hdb <- sum(on_hdb)
priv <- osm_pts[!on_hdb, ] |> st_join(select(sz, SZ), join = st_intersects)

# Dormitories are left out: their occupants are mostly foreign workers and students
# who are not in the resident count. They are carried as a separate market in
# 02_stations.R.
condo_types  <- c("apartments", "residential")
landed_types <- c("house", "terrace", "semidetached_house", "detached", "bungalow")
cand <- bind_rows(
  priv |> filter(type %in% condo_types)  |> mutate(group = "condo",  w = area),
  priv |> filter(type %in% landed_types) |> mutate(group = "landed", w = 1)
)

# "Others" (shophouses, attap and so on) has no building type of its own, and is
# treated with condominiums. Where a subzone has residents but no candidate of the
# right type, the other private type is tried, then OSM residential land, and
# finally the subzone's interior, each of which is counted in the audit.
pop_priv <- pop |>
  filter(group %in% c("condo", "landed", "other")) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(group == "other", "condo", group)) |>
  group_by(SZ, group) |>
  summarise(Pop = sum(Pop), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(Pop > 0)

landuse <- st_read(paste0(Z, "gis_osm_landuse_a_free_1.shp"), wkt_filter = bb, quiet = TRUE) |>
  filter(fclass == "residential") |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(SVY21)
landuse$w <- as.numeric(st_area(landuse))
lu_pts <- st_point_on_surface(landuse) |> st_join(select(sz, SZ), join = st_intersects)

allocate_private <- function(s, g, p) {
  this <- cand |> filter(SZ == s, group == g)
  tier <- "same type"
  if (nrow(this) == 0) { this <- cand |> filter(SZ == s); tier <- "other private type" }
  if (nrow(this) == 0) { this <- lu_pts |> filter(SZ == s); tier <- "OSM residential land" }
  if (nrow(this) == 0) {
    this <- st_sf(w = 1, geometry = st_point_on_surface(st_geometry(sz[sz$SZ == s, ])))
    tier <- "subzone interior"
  }
  xy <- st_coordinates(this)
  tibble(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2], res = p * this$w / sum(this$w), tier = tier, group = g, SZ = s)
}
priv_res <- bind_rows(Map(allocate_private, pop_priv$SZ, pop_priv$group, pop_priv$Pop))
audit$priv_total <- sum(priv_res$res)
audit$priv_by_tier <- priv_res |> group_by(tier) |> summarise(res = sum(res), .groups = "drop")

# ---- Hexagon grid -----------------------------------------------------------
# Hexagons are equidistant from their six neighbours and small enough for a walk
# to a station to differ across them. Each hexagon's distance point is its
# population-weighted centre rather than its geometric centre, which removes most
# of the error of treating a cell as a point.
hex <- st_make_grid(land, cellsize = HEX_M, square = FALSE) |>
  st_sf(geometry = _)
hex <- hex[lengths(st_intersects(hex, land)) > 0, ]
hex$hex_id <- sprintf("H%04d", seq_len(nrow(hex)))
audit$hex_n <- nrow(hex)

hdb_pts <- blocks |>
  filter(year_completed <= 2025) |>
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  st_join(select(hex, hex_id), join = st_intersects) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id, x, y, res, du = total_dwelling_units)

priv_pts <- priv_res |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = SVY21, remove = FALSE) |>
  st_join(select(hex, hex_id), join = st_nearest_feature) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id, x, y, res)

people <- bind_rows(mutate(hdb_pts, src = "hdb"), mutate(priv_pts, src = "private", du = 0))

hex_tot <- people |>
  group_by(hex_id) |>
  summarise(wx = sum(x * res) / sum(res), wy = sum(y * res) / sum(res),
            residents = sum(res),
            res_hdb = sum(res[src == "hdb"]), res_private = sum(res[src == "private"]),
            hdb_du = sum(du), .groups = "drop")

hex <- hex |>
  left_join(hex_tot, by = "hex_id") |>
  mutate(across(c(residents, res_hdb, res_private, hdb_du), \(v) coalesce(v, 0)))
hex_c <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(hex)))
hex <- hex |>
  mutate(cx = hex_c[, 1], cy = hex_c[, 2],
         x = coalesce(wx, cx), y = coalesce(wy, cy)) |>
  select(-wx, -wy, -cx, -cy)
# A hexagon can straddle subzones, so it is labelled by its population-weighted
# centre rather than by whichever subzone its polygon meets first.
hex_lab <- st_as_sf(st_drop_geometry(hex), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = SVY21) |>
  st_join(select(sz, SZ, PA, REGION), join = st_nearest_feature) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id, SZ, PA, REGION)
hex <- left_join(hex, hex_lab, by = "hex_id")

audit$res_in_hex <- sum(hex$residents)
audit$hex_populated <- sum(hex$residents > 0)
audit$share_private <- sum(hex$res_private) / sum(hex$residents)

# Blocks completed in 2026, kept for the 2030 scenario.
new_2026 <- blocks |>
  filter(year_completed == 2026) |>
  select(blk, street, res, du = total_dwelling_units)

saveRDS(sz, file.path(DER, "subzone.rds"))
saveRDS(st_union(sz), file.path(DER, "land.rds"))
saveRDS(blocks, file.path(DER, "hdb_blocks.rds"))
saveRDS(crosswalk, file.path(DER, "street_crosswalk.rds"))
saveRDS(new_2026, file.path(DER, "hdb_new_2026.rds"))
saveRDS(hex, file.path(DER, "hex.rds"))
saveRDS(select(people, x, y, res, src, du), file.path(DER, "people_points.rds"))
saveRDS(audit, file.path(DER, "audit_markets.rds"))

str(audit, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
scripts/02_stations.R 
# =============================================================================
# 02_stations.R -- destinations: existing and proposed stations, and their pull
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# A station is a place, not a code. An interchange has several codes, and a future
# line can bring a new code to a station that already exists, so codes are first
# collapsed into physical stations. The attraction variables are then measured
# around each station, on the same definitions for existing and proposed ones,
# because a proposed station has nothing else to be predicted from.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex3/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(stringr); library(purrr)
})
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

RAW <- "data/raw"; DER <- "data/derived"; SVY21 <- 3414
audit <- list()
land <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "land.rds"))
hex  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "hex.rds"))

# ---- LTA station layer ------------------------------------------------------
# Station identifiers sit in STN_NAM as codes, and the layer's SVY21 definition has
# no EPSG code. It also holds depots and ancillary buildings with no passengers
# (their codes are not station codes), several polygons for some single stations,
# and shared polygons named "EW24 / NS1".
ly <- st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", RAW, "/lta/TrainStation_Sep2026.zip/TrainStation_Sep2026/",
                     "RapidTransitSystemStation.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_set_crs(NA) |> st_set_crs(SVY21) |>
  st_make_valid()
audit$layer_n <- nrow(ly)
audit$layer_dup <- st_drop_geometry(ly) |> count(STN_NAM) |> filter(n > 1)
audit$layer_shared <- ly$STN_NAM[grepl("/", ly$STN_NAM)]

is_station_code <- function(x) str_detect(x, "^(NS|EW|CG|NE|CC|CE|DT|TE|BP|SE|SW|PE|PW|STC|PTC)[0-9]*[A-Z]?$")
ly_codes <- st_drop_geometry(ly) |>
  mutate(code = str_split(STN_NAM, "\\s*/\\s*")) |>
  unnest(code) |>
  mutate(code = str_trim(code))
audit$layer_nonstation <- sort(unique(ly_codes$code[!is_station_code(ly_codes$code)]))
layer_codes <- unique(ly_codes$code[is_station_code(ly_codes$code)])

# ---- Station lists ----------------------------------------------------------
# The coordinate lists carry a code, a name and a point for every station, built
# from URA's Master Plan. They date from March 2026, so three stations they call
# future (Circle Line Stage 6) had opened by the September layer and the OD months.
op <- read_csv(file.path(RAW, "stations/operational_stations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
fu <- read_csv(file.path(RAW, "stations/future_stations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
all_codes <- bind_rows(mutate(op, listed = "operational"), mutate(fu, listed = "future")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(SVY21) |>
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2],
         line = str_extract(station_code, "^[A-Z]+")) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

audit$codes_operational <- nrow(op)
audit$codes_future <- nrow(fu)
audit$op_not_in_layer <- setdiff(op$station_code, layer_codes)
audit$future_in_layer <- intersect(fu$station_code, layer_codes)

# What each code is, as of the September 2026 layer and LTA's project pages.
# The handout's proposed stations are the Jurong Region Line stations opening by
# 2029 (24, leaving out the mid-2030s infill at JS2A) and Cross Island Line Phase 1
# (12 stations, CR2 to CR13, 2030).
CCL6    <- c("CC30", "CC31", "CC32")
SHELLS  <- c("CC18", "TE10", "TE21", "TE22A")
JRL     <- c(paste0("JS", 1:12), paste0("JE", 1:7), paste0("JW", 1:5))
CRL1    <- paste0("CR", 2:13)
all_codes <- all_codes |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    listed == "operational" | station_code %in% CCL6 ~ "open",
    station_code %in% SHELLS ~ "shell",
    station_code %in% c(JRL, CRL1) ~ "proposed",
    TRUE ~ "later"))

# ---- Physical stations ------------------------------------------------------
# Codes sharing a name are one station. The check below confirms that the name
# never joins two places: the largest gap inside a name is reported in the audit.
gap <- all_codes |>
  group_by(station_name) |>
  summarise(n = n(), gap_m = max(as.numeric(dist(cbind(x, y))), 0), .groups = "drop")
audit$name_gap <- gap |> filter(n > 1) |> arrange(desc(gap_m)) |> head(12)

# An existing station's position stays as it is when a future line arrives: a
# passenger reaches the same entrances, so the new code adds a line and not a place.
stations <- all_codes |>
  mutate(rank_status = match(status, c("open", "shell", "proposed", "later"))) |>
  group_by(station_name) |>
  summarise(
    codes_all = paste(station_code, collapse = "/"),
    lines_now      = n_distinct(line[status == "open"]),
    lines_proposed = n_distinct(line[status %in% c("open", "proposed")]),
    is_lrt_only    = any(status == "open") &&
      all(line[status == "open"] %in% c("BP", "SE", "SW", "PE", "PW", "STC", "PTC")),
    has_new_code   = any(status == "proposed"),
    x = mean(x[rank_status == min(rank_status)]),
    y = mean(y[rank_status == min(rank_status)]),
    # Assigned last: from here on, `status` would mean the station's, not the code's.
    status    = status[which.min(rank_status)],
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(station_id = sprintf("S%03d", row_number()),
         # LRT stations and MRT lines count as one mode change each
         is_interchange_now = lines_now >= 2,
         role = case_when(
           status == "open" & has_new_code ~ "existing, gains a line",
           status == "open" ~ "existing",
           status == "proposed" ~ "new access point",
           status == "shell" ~ "built, not open",
           TRUE ~ "after 2030"))
audit$role_counts <- count(stations, role)
audit$proposed_codes_n <- sum(all_codes$station_code %in% c(JRL, CRL1))

code_map <- all_codes |>
  select(station_code, station_name, line, status) |>
  left_join(select(stations, station_name, station_id), by = "station_name")

st_pts <- stations |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = SVY21, remove = FALSE)

# ---- Attraction variables ---------------------------------------------------
Z  <- paste0("/vsizip/", RAW, "/osm/malaysia-singapore-brunei-latest-free.shp.zip/")
bb <- st_as_text(st_as_sfc(st_bbox(st_transform(st_as_sf(land), 4326))))
read_osm <- function(l) {
  st_read(paste0(Z, l, ".shp"), wkt_filter = bb, quiet = TRUE) |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_transform(SVY21)
}

# Bus stops. The file has 21 codes entered twice and five stops across the Causeway
# in Johor Bahru, which are removed; a stop's own code is what makes it one stop.
bus <- st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", RAW, "/lta/BusStopLocation_Mar2026.zip/",
                      "BusStopLocation_Mar2026/BusStop.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_set_crs(NA) |> st_set_crs(SVY21)
audit$bus_n <- nrow(bus)
audit$bus_dup <- sum(duplicated(bus$BUS_STOP_N))
out <- lengths(st_intersects(bus, st_buffer(land, 100))) == 0
audit$bus_outside <- st_drop_geometry(bus)[out, c("BUS_STOP_N", "LOC_DESC")]
bus <- bus[!out, ] |> distinct(BUS_STOP_N, .keep_all = TRUE)
audit$bus_clean <- nrow(bus)

# Points of interest, grouped into the kinds of trip they generate. Street furniture
# that OSM also records (benches, waste baskets, vending machines) is left out.
POI_GROUPS <- list(
  food    = c("restaurant", "cafe", "fast_food", "food_court", "bar", "pub", "biergarten"),
  retail  = c("mall", "supermarket", "convenience", "department_store", "clothes", "shoe_shop",
              "jeweller", "optician", "beauty_shop", "furniture_shop", "bakery", "doityourself",
              "general", "gift_shop", "bookshop", "computer_shop", "mobile_phone_shop",
              "sports_shop", "toy_shop", "stationery", "florist", "marketplace", "beverages",
              "butcher", "greengrocer", "kiosk", "chemist", "garden_centre", "outdoor_shop",
              "bicycle_shop", "car_dealership", "hairdresser", "laundry", "bank", "travel_agent"),
  civic   = c("hospital", "clinic", "doctors", "dentist", "pharmacy", "nursing_home", "veterinary",
              "school", "college", "university", "kindergarten", "library", "community_centre",
              "courthouse", "town_hall", "post_office", "police", "fire_station", "embassy"),
  leisure = c("attraction", "museum", "theatre", "cinema", "arts_centre", "zoo", "theme_park",
              "stadium", "sports_centre", "fitness_centre", "hotel", "hostel", "guesthouse",
              "motel", "nightclub", "golf_course", "swimming_pool"))
poi_lookup <- tibble(group = rep(names(POI_GROUPS), lengths(POI_GROUPS)),
                     fclass = unlist(POI_GROUPS))
poi <- bind_rows(
  read_osm("gis_osm_pois_free_1") |> select(osm_id, fclass),
  read_osm("gis_osm_pois_a_free_1") |> select(osm_id, fclass) |> st_point_on_surface()
) |>
  st_filter(land) |>
  inner_join(poi_lookup, by = "fclass")
audit$poi_n <- nrow(poi)
audit$poi_by_group <- st_drop_geometry(poi) |> count(group)

# Floor space for work and retail. OSM has no heights, so this is footprint, which
# understates the tall offices of the CBD; that bias is examined in the report.
WORK_TYPES <- c("commercial", "office", "retail", "industrial", "warehouse", "hotel", "public",
                "government", "hospital", "school", "university", "college", "supermarket")
osm_b <- read_osm("gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1") |> select(type)
osm_b$area <- as.numeric(st_area(osm_b))
work <- osm_b |>
  filter(type %in% WORK_TYPES) |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  st_filter(land)
audit$work_n <- nrow(work)

# Dormitories house people the resident count leaves out: foreign workers above all,
# and students. OSM is the only available record of where they are.
dorm <- osm_b |>
  filter(type == "dormitory") |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  st_filter(land)
audit$dorm_n <- nrow(dorm)

lu <- read_osm("gis_osm_landuse_a_free_1") |>
  filter(fclass %in% c("commercial", "retail", "industrial")) |>
  st_intersection(st_as_sf(land)) |>
  select(fclass)

count_within <- function(pts, centres, r) lengths(st_intersects(st_buffer(centres, r), pts))
sum_within <- function(pts, val, centres, r) {
  hits <- st_intersects(st_buffer(centres, r), pts)
  vapply(hits, function(i) sum(val[i]), numeric(1))
}
lu_area_within <- function(centres, r) {
  buf <- st_buffer(centres, r) |> select(station_id)
  st_intersection(buf, st_geometry(st_as_sf(st_union(lu)))) |>
    mutate(a = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(station_id) |>
    summarise(a = sum(a), .groups = "drop") |>
    right_join(st_drop_geometry(buf), by = "station_id") |>
    mutate(a = coalesce(a, 0)) |>
    arrange(match(station_id, buf$station_id)) |>
    pull(a)
}

hex_pts <- hex |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(residents > 0) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = SVY21)

RAFFLES <- all_codes |> filter(station_name == "Raffles Place") |> summarise(x = mean(x), y = mean(y))

attr_tbl <- st_pts |>
  transmute(
    station_id,
    bus_400     = count_within(bus, geometry, 400),
    food_400    = count_within(filter(poi, group == "food"), geometry, 400),
    retail_400  = count_within(filter(poi, group == "retail"), geometry, 400),
    civic_400   = count_within(filter(poi, group == "civic"), geometry, 400),
    leisure_400 = count_within(filter(poi, group == "leisure"), geometry, 400),
    poi_800     = count_within(poi, geometry, 800),
    work_m2_400 = sum_within(work, work$area, geometry, 400),
    work_m2_800 = sum_within(work, work$area, geometry, 800),
    res_400     = sum_within(hex_pts, hex_pts$residents, geometry, 400),
    res_800     = sum_within(hex_pts, hex_pts$residents, geometry, 800),
    km_cbd      = sqrt((x - RAFFLES$x)^2 + (y - RAFFLES$y)^2) / 1000
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
attr_tbl$lu_m2_400 <- lu_area_within(select(st_pts, station_id), 400)

stations_full <- stations |>
  left_join(attr_tbl, by = "station_id")

# ---- Origin-side activity ---------------------------------------------------
# The second market. Tap-ins away from home come from people returning from work,
# school and shops, so each hexagon also carries the activity located in it.
hex_poly <- select(hex, hex_id)
add_hex <- function(pts, val = NULL) {
  j <- st_join(pts, hex_poly, join = st_intersects) |> st_drop_geometry()
  j$v <- if (is.null(val)) 1 else val
  j |> filter(!is.na(hex_id)) |> group_by(hex_id) |> summarise(v = sum(v), .groups = "drop")
}
activity <- select(st_drop_geometry(hex), hex_id) |>
  left_join(rename(add_hex(poi), poi = v), by = "hex_id") |>
  left_join(rename(add_hex(work, work$area), work_m2 = v), by = "hex_id") |>
  left_join(rename(add_hex(dorm, dorm$area), dorm_m2 = v), by = "hex_id") |>
  mutate(across(c(poi, work_m2, dorm_m2), \(v) coalesce(v, 0)))
hex2 <- left_join(hex, activity, by = "hex_id")
audit$hex_with_market <- sum(hex2$residents > 0 | hex2$poi > 0 | hex2$work_m2 > 0 | hex2$dorm_m2 > 0)

saveRDS(stations_full, file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
saveRDS(code_map, file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds"))
saveRDS(hex2, file.path(DER, "hex_markets.rds"))
activity_pts <- bind_rows(
  mutate(st_drop_geometry(work), x = st_coordinates(work)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(work)[, 2], kind = "work"),
  mutate(st_drop_geometry(dorm), x = st_coordinates(dorm)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(dorm)[, 2], kind = "dorm"),
  mutate(st_drop_geometry(poi), x = st_coordinates(poi)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(poi)[, 2], area = 1, kind = "poi")
) |> select(x, y, area, kind)
saveRDS(activity_pts, file.path(DER, "activity_points.rds"))
saveRDS(audit, file.path(DER, "audit_stations.rds"))

str(audit, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
print(audit$name_gap); print(audit$role_counts); print(audit$poi_by_group)
print(as.data.frame(stations_full |> filter(role %in% c("existing, gains a line", "built, not open")) |>
                      select(station_name, codes_all, role, lines_now, lines_proposed)))
print(summary(select(stations_full, bus_400, food_400, retail_400, civic_400, leisure_400, work_m2_400, res_800, lu_m2_400)))
scripts/03_ridership.R 
# =============================================================================
# 03_ridership.R -- observed ridership at each physical station
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# Reads the DataMall passenger volumes for July to September 2026, merges the
# several codes a station can appear under, converts monthly totals to average
# daily volumes, and reconciles the OD file against the station file.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex3/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(stringr); library(purrr)
})

RAW <- "data/raw/lta"; DER <- "data/derived"
audit <- list()
MONTHS <- c("202607", "202608", "202609")

read_zip <- function(prefix, inner, m, types) {
  read_csv(unz(file.path(RAW, sprintf("%s_%s.zip", prefix, m)), sprintf("%s_%s.csv", inner, m)),
           show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = types)
}
node <- map_dfr(MONTHS, \(m) read_zip("PVTrain", "transport_node_train", m, "cciccdd"))
od   <- map_dfr(MONTHS, \(m) read_zip("PVODTrain", "origin_destination_train", m, "cciccci") |>
                  mutate(TOTAL_TRIPS = as.numeric(TOTAL_TRIPS)))
audit$node_rows <- nrow(node)
audit$od_rows   <- nrow(od)

# ---- Codes to physical stations ---------------------------------------------
# A node code joins the station codes of an interchange ("NS24/NE6/CC1"). Three
# stations appear under two node codes. Circle Line Stage 6 renumbered Marina Bay
# and Bayfront (CE2 to CC33, CE1 to CC34) when it opened on 12 July 2026, so both
# spellings are in the July file; and Stevens is reported as two separate nodes for
# its two lines, DT10 and TE11. The renumbered codes are not in the March
# coordinate list and are added here.
code_map <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds")) |>
  select(code = station_code, station_id, station_name)
extra <- code_map |>
  filter(code %in% c("CE2", "CE1")) |>
  mutate(code = recode(code, CE2 = "CC33", CE1 = "CC34"))
code_map <- bind_rows(code_map, extra)

raw_codes <- tibble(raw = unique(c(node$PT_CODE, od$ORIGIN_PT_CODE, od$DESTINATION_PT_CODE))) |>
  mutate(code = str_split(raw, "[^A-Z0-9]+")) |>
  unnest(code)
lookup <- raw_codes |>
  left_join(code_map, by = "code") |>
  group_by(raw) |>
  summarise(n_st = n_distinct(station_id), unmatched = any(is.na(station_id)),
            station_id = first(station_id), station_name = first(station_name), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(lookup$n_st == 1), !any(lookup$unmatched))
audit$raw_codes <- nrow(lookup)
audit$stations  <- n_distinct(lookup$station_id)
audit$multi_node <- lookup |>
  group_by(station_name) |>
  summarise(codes = paste(raw, collapse = " + "), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n > 1)

# ---- Calendar -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Monthly totals are not comparable, because the months have different numbers of
# each kind of day. August 2026 has 20 weekdays against July's 23: National Day
# falls on a Sunday, so Monday 10 August is a public holiday.
calendar <- tibble(date = seq(as.Date("2026-07-01"), as.Date("2026-09-30"), by = "day")) |>
  mutate(YEAR_MONTH = format(date, "%Y-%m"),
         dow = as.integer(format(date, "%u")),
         DAY_TYPE = ifelse(dow >= 6 | date == as.Date("2026-08-10"), "WEEKENDS/HOLIDAY", "WEEKDAY")) |>
  count(YEAR_MONTH, DAY_TYPE, name = "days")
audit$calendar <- calendar

audit$month_check <- node |>
  group_by(YEAR_MONTH, DAY_TYPE) |>
  summarise(tap_in = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(calendar, by = c("YEAR_MONTH", "DAY_TYPE")) |>
  mutate(per_day = tap_in / days)

# ---- Reference period ---------------------------------------------------------
# July is left out of the calibration: Circle Line Stage 6 opened on 12 July, so its
# stations have a partial month, and the rest of the network was adjusting to a
# closed circle. August and September describe one stable network.
REF <- c("2026-08", "2026-09")
ref_days <- calendar |>
  filter(YEAR_MONTH %in% REF) |>
  group_by(DAY_TYPE) |>
  summarise(days = sum(days), .groups = "drop")
n_wd <- ref_days$days[ref_days$DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY"]
n_we <- ref_days$days[ref_days$DAY_TYPE != "WEEKDAY"]
audit$ref_days <- ref_days

per <- function(h) case_when(h %in% 6:8 ~ "am", h %in% 17:19 ~ "pm", TRUE ~ "off")

rid <- node |>
  filter(YEAR_MONTH %in% REF) |>
  left_join(select(lookup, raw, station_id), by = c("PT_CODE" = "raw")) |>
  mutate(period = per(TIME_PER_HOUR)) |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(
    # Average day across the reference period, weighting weekdays and weekends by how
    # many of each a typical week holds, so that the calendar does not matter.
    wd_in  = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY"]) / n_wd,
    we_in  = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE != "WEEKDAY"]) / n_we,
    wd_out = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY"]) / n_wd,
    we_out = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE != "WEEKDAY"]) / n_we,
    am_in  = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY" & period == "am"]) / n_wd,
    pm_in  = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY" & period == "pm"]) / n_wd,
    am_out = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY" & period == "am"]) / n_wd,
    pm_out = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY" & period == "pm"]) / n_wd,
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(daily_in  = (5 * wd_in + 2 * we_in) / 7,
         daily_out = (5 * wd_out + 2 * we_out) / 7)
audit$daily_total <- sum(rid$daily_in)
audit$wd_total    <- sum(rid$wd_in)
audit$we_total    <- sum(rid$we_in)

# Whether the months differ at station level: a stability check on the reference.
stab <- node |>
  left_join(select(lookup, raw, station_id), by = c("PT_CODE" = "raw")) |>
  left_join(calendar, by = c("YEAR_MONTH", "DAY_TYPE")) |>
  group_by(YEAR_MONTH, DAY_TYPE, station_id) |>
  summarise(v = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME) / first(days), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY") |>
  select(-DAY_TYPE) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = YEAR_MONTH, values_from = v)
audit$stab_aug_sep_cor <- cor(log(stab$`2026-08`), log(stab$`2026-09`))
audit$stab_aug_sep_mape <- median(abs(stab$`2026-09` / stab$`2026-08` - 1))

# ---- OD against the station file ----------------------------------------------
# The OD file records completed journeys, so it should fall a little short of tap-ins.
od_o <- od |> group_by(YEAR_MONTH, raw = ORIGIN_PT_CODE) |> summarise(od_o = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS), .groups = "drop")
od_d <- od |> group_by(YEAR_MONTH, raw = DESTINATION_PT_CODE) |> summarise(od_d = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS), .groups = "drop")
rec <- node |>
  group_by(YEAR_MONTH, raw = PT_CODE) |>
  summarise(tin = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME), tout = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME), .groups = "drop") |>
  full_join(od_o, by = c("YEAR_MONTH", "raw")) |>
  full_join(od_d, by = c("YEAR_MONTH", "raw")) |>
  mutate(r_in = od_o / tin, r_out = od_d / tout)
audit$od_to_node <- sum(rec$od_o) / sum(rec$tin)
audit$od_ratio_range <- range(rec$r_in)
audit$od_ratio_low <- rec |> arrange(r_in) |> head(5) |> select(YEAR_MONTH, raw, tin, od_o, r_in)
audit$od_selfloop <- sum(od$TOTAL_TRIPS[od$ORIGIN_PT_CODE == od$DESTINATION_PT_CODE])

# ---- Station-to-station flows -------------------------------------------------
# Used by the destination-choice model. Average daily trips over the reference
# period, by the same day weighting as above.
od_st <- od |>
  filter(YEAR_MONTH %in% REF) |>
  left_join(select(lookup, raw, o = station_id), by = c("ORIGIN_PT_CODE" = "raw")) |>
  left_join(select(lookup, raw, d = station_id), by = c("DESTINATION_PT_CODE" = "raw")) |>
  mutate(period = per(TIME_PER_HOUR)) |>
  group_by(o, d) |>
  summarise(wd = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY"]) / n_wd,
            we = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS[DAY_TYPE != "WEEKDAY"]) / n_we,
            am = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS[DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY" & period == "am"]) / n_wd,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(daily = (5 * wd + 2 * we) / 7) |>
  filter(o != d)
audit$od_pairs <- nrow(od_st)
audit$od_pairs_possible <- audit$stations * (audit$stations - 1)

saveRDS(rid, file.path(DER, "ridership.rds"))
saveRDS(od_st, file.path(DER, "od_station.rds"))
saveRDS(audit, file.path(DER, "audit_ridership.rds"))

str(audit, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
print(audit$month_check); print(audit$multi_node); print(audit$od_ratio_low)
scripts/04_frames.R 
# =============================================================================
# 04_frames.R -- the spatial interaction data frames the brief asks for
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# Two interaction frames (existing network; existing plus proposed), one table of
# origins with their local market potential, and one table of destinations with
# observed ridership and attraction variables. The origin and destination columns
# carry the same names in all of them, as MCI's functions require.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex3/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(igraph)
})
source("R/rail.R")
DER <- "data/derived"
FLOOR_KM <- 0.1   # a hexagon's point can sit on a station; decay needs a positive distance

hex <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "hex_markets.rds")) |> st_drop_geometry()
st  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
rid <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ridership.rds"))

# ---- Origins ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only hexagons holding some market can send anyone to a station.
origins <- hex |>
  filter(residents > 0 | work_m2 > 0 | dorm_m2 > 0) |>
  transmute(origin = hex_id, x, y, SZ, PA, REGION, residents, res_hdb, res_private,
            hdb_du, poi, work_m2, dorm_m2)

# ---- Destinations -------------------------------------------------------------
# The attraction variables are logged, so that each coefficient reads as an
# elasticity, and centred on the existing network, so that a station at the network's
# average has an attractiveness of one.
transform_x <- function(d) {
  d |> mutate(l_bus  = log1p(bus_400),
              l_ret  = log1p(retail_400),
              l_food = log1p(food_400),
              l_civ  = log1p(civic_400),
              l_lei  = log1p(leisure_400),
              l_work = log1p(work_m2_400 / 1000),
              l_res8 = log1p(res_800))
}
st <- transform_x(st)

dest_existing <- st |>
  filter(status == "open") |>
  left_join(rid, by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(lrt = as.numeric(is_lrt_only),
         ic  = pmax(lines_now - 1, 0),
         # Two kinds of tap-in. In the morning peak a station's tap-ins are people
         # leaving home and its tap-outs are people arriving at work or study, so the
         # balance between them says what share of its ridership starts from home.
         # Raffles Place is near 0 and Buangkok near 1. The rest of its ridership is
         # the return leg, tapping in near work, school or shops.
         phi = am_in / (am_in + am_out),
         T_H = daily_in * phi,
         T_W = daily_in * (1 - phi)) |>
  arrange(station_id) |>
  rename(destination = station_id)
stopifnot(!anyNA(dest_existing$daily_in))

# The second destination table describes the network once the proposed lines are in
# place. New access points have no ridership yet. They are classed as MRT: the Cross
# Island Line is heavy rail, and the Jurong Region Line, though medium capacity, runs
# as a separate line with its own codes, which a sensitivity test relaxes. An
# existing station that gains a line stays where it is, with one more line.
dest_proposed <- st |>
  filter(status == "open" | role == "new access point") |>
  left_join(rid, by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(lrt = as.numeric(is_lrt_only & status == "open"),
         ic  = ifelse(status == "open", pmax(lines_proposed - 1, 0), 0)) |>
  arrange(station_id) |>
  rename(destination = station_id)

# ---- Rail time to the CBD ------------------------------------------------------
# A station's pull depends on where it leads as well as on what surrounds it, and a
# station that needs a transfer to reach the city is worth less than one on a through
# line. Rail time to Raffles Place, with a penalty for each change, carries that. The
# proposed lines shorten it for some existing stations as well, so it is recomputed.
cx <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds")) |>
  left_join(select(st, station_id, x, y), by = "station_id") |>
  select(code = station_code, station_id, station_name, x, y)
g_old <- build_graph(NETWORK, cx)
g_new <- build_graph(c(NETWORK, PROPOSED), cx)
RM_old <- rail_matrix(g_old, dest_existing$destination)
RM_new <- rail_matrix(g_new, dest_proposed$destination)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(RM_old)), all(is.finite(RM_new)))
cbd <- dest_existing$destination[dest_existing$station_name == "Raffles Place"]
dest_existing <- mutate(dest_existing, min_cbd = pmax(RM_old[, cbd], 1), l_cbd = log(min_cbd))
dest_proposed <- mutate(dest_proposed, min_cbd = pmax(RM_new[, cbd], 1), l_cbd = log(min_cbd))

X_VARS <- c("l_bus", "l_ret", "l_food", "lrt", "ic", "l_cbd")
centre <- colMeans(dest_existing[, X_VARS])

# ---- Interaction frames -------------------------------------------------------
pairs_for <- function(dst) {
  d <- sqrt(outer(origins$x, dst$x, "-")^2 + outer(origins$y, dst$y, "-")^2) / 1000
  d[d < FLOOR_KM] <- FLOOR_KM
  dimnames(d) <- list(origins$origin, dst$destination)
  d
}
D_existing <- pairs_for(dest_existing)
D_proposed <- pairs_for(dest_proposed)

as_frame <- function(D) {
  tibble(origin = rep(rownames(D), times = ncol(D)),
         destination = rep(colnames(D), each = nrow(D)),
         distance = as.vector(D))
}
si_existing <- as_frame(D_existing)
si_proposed <- as_frame(D_proposed)

audit <- list(
  n_origins = nrow(origins),
  n_origins_residents = sum(origins$residents > 0),
  n_existing = nrow(dest_existing),
  n_new = sum(dest_proposed$role == "new access point"),
  n_gains = sum(dest_proposed$role == "existing, gains a line"),
  n_pairs_existing = nrow(si_existing),
  n_pairs_proposed = nrow(si_proposed),
  res_by_nearest = with(list(nearest = apply(D_existing, 1, min)),
    round(tapply(origins$residents, cut(nearest, c(0, .4, .8, 1.2, 2, 3, 30)), sum) /
            sum(origins$residents), 4)),
  res_by_nearest_new = with(list(nearest = apply(D_proposed, 1, min)),
    round(tapply(origins$residents, cut(nearest, c(0, .4, .8, 1.2, 2, 3, 30)), sum) /
            sum(origins$residents), 4)),
  X_VARS = X_VARS,
  centre = centre
)

saveRDS(origins, file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
saveRDS(dest_existing, file.path(DER, "dest_existing.rds"))
saveRDS(dest_proposed, file.path(DER, "dest_proposed.rds"))
saveRDS(si_existing, file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds"))
saveRDS(si_proposed, file.path(DER, "si_proposed.rds"))
saveRDS(D_existing, file.path(DER, "D_existing.rds"))
saveRDS(D_proposed, file.path(DER, "D_proposed.rds"))
saveRDS(RM_old, file.path(DER, "RM_existing.rds"))
saveRDS(RM_new, file.path(DER, "RM_proposed.rds"))
saveRDS(audit, file.path(DER, "audit_frames.rds"))
str(audit, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
print(audit$res_by_nearest); print(audit$res_by_nearest_new)
scripts/05_calibrate.R 
# =============================================================================
# 05_calibrate.R -- calibrating the model, and testing it against simpler ones
# Take-home Exercise 3 | ISSS626
#
# A ladder of models from the nearest-station rule upwards. Each is scored in sample
# and by leaving out one line at a time, which is the closest available imitation of
# the real task: predicting a line the model has never seen, with its stations absent
# from the network during calibration. The selected model is then profiled, tested
# against a permutation null, bootstrapped, and checked against MCI.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex3/. About 15 minutes on 8 workers.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(spdep); library(sf); library(parallel); library(MCI)
})
source("R/utils.R"); source("R/huff.R")
DER <- "data/derived"
set.seed(1234)
N_WORKERS <- 8
N_BOOT <- 300
DMAX <- 5   # km; the choice set stops here (the profile below shows why)

origins <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
dest    <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "dest_existing.rds"))
dP      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "dest_proposed.rds"))
codes   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds"))
D       <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "D_existing.rds"))
Dn      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "D_proposed.rds"))
AF      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "audit_frames.rds"))
X_VARS  <- AF$X_VARS
X_BASE  <- setdiff(X_VARS, "l_cbd")
idx_old <- match(dest$destination, dP$destination)
idx_new <- which(dP$role == "new access point")

# Each market column is scaled to the same total as residents, so that its kappa says
# how many tap-ins a resident-equivalent unit of it generates relative to the others.
TOT <- sum(origins$residents)
nz  <- function(v) v / sum(v) * TOT
MH  <- cbind(residents = origins$residents, dorm = nz(origins$dorm_m2))
MW  <- cbind(work = nz(origins$work_m2), poi = nz(origins$poi))
M3  <- cbind(residents = origins$residents, work = nz(origins$work_m2), dorm = nz(origins$dorm_m2))
M1  <- cbind(residents = origins$residents)

mkX <- function(vars, d = dest) {
  if (!length(vars)) return(matrix(0, nrow(d), 0))
  sweep(as.matrix(d[, vars, drop = FALSE]), 2, AF$centre[vars], "-")
}

# ---- Folds ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A station is held out with a line only if it serves no other line; interchanges stay.
folds <- codes |>
  filter(status == "open", station_id %in% dest$destination) |>
  mutate(g = case_when(line %in% c("EW", "CG") ~ "EW",
                       line %in% c("CC", "CE") ~ "CC",
                       line == "BP" ~ "LRT Bukit Panjang",
                       line %in% c("SE", "SW", "STC") ~ "LRT Sengkang",
                       line %in% c("PE", "PW", "PTC") ~ "LRT Punggol",
                       TRUE ~ line)) |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(n = n_distinct(g), fold = first(g), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n == 1) |>
  select(destination = station_id, fold)
dest <- left_join(dest, folds, by = "destination")
FOLDS <- sort(setdiff(unique(dest$fold), NA))

make_spec <- function(Tv, M, vars = X_VARS, type = "pow", dmax = DMAX, use_A0 = FALSE) {
  list(D = D, T = Tv, M = M, X = mkX(vars), type = type, dmax = dmax, use_A0 = use_A0)
}

lolo_part <- function(spec, fix_lambda = NULL) {
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, ncol(D))
  for (f in FOLDS) {
    te <- which(dest$fold == f); tr <- setdiff(seq_len(ncol(D)), te)
    s2 <- modifyList(spec, list(D = D[, tr, drop = FALSE], X = spec$X[tr, , drop = FALSE], T = spec$T[tr]))
    fit <- fit_huff(s2, fix_lambda = fix_lambda)
    pred[te] <- expected(fit$par, s2, D = D, X = spec$X)[te]
  }
  pred
}

stats_row <- function(name, group, E, pred, lambda, n_par) {
  ok <- !is.na(pred); T <- dest$daily_in
  tibble(model = name, group = group, lambda = lambda, n_par = n_par,
         insample = fit_stats(T, E)$r2_log, insample_rho = fit_stats(T, E)$rho,
         lolo_r2 = fit_stats(T[ok], pred[ok])$r2_log, lolo_rmsle = fit_stats(T[ok], pred[ok])$rmsle,
         lolo_mape = fit_stats(T[ok], pred[ok])$mape, lolo_rho = fit_stats(T[ok], pred[ok])$rho)
}

# Single-purpose: one model of all tap-ins.
score_one <- function(d) {
  sp <- make_spec(dest$daily_in, d$M, d$vars, d$type %||% "pow", d$dmax %||% Inf, d$use_A0 %||% FALSE)
  fit <- fit_huff(sp, fix_lambda = d$fix)
  pred <- lolo_part(sp, d$fix)
  list(name = d$name, group = d$group, fit = fit, lolo = pred,
       row = stats_row(d$name, d$group, fit$E, pred, fit$par[1], length(fit$par)))
}
# Two-purpose: the home end and the activity end, calibrated separately and summed.
score_two <- function(d) {
  sh <- make_spec(dest$T_H, d$MH %||% MH, d$vars, d$type %||% "pow", d$dmax %||% DMAX, d$use_A0 %||% FALSE)
  sw <- make_spec(dest$T_W, d$MW %||% MW, d$vars, d$type %||% "pow", d$dmax %||% DMAX, FALSE)
  fh <- fit_huff(sh, fix_lambda = d$fix); fw <- fit_huff(sw, fix_lambda = d$fix)
  ph <- lolo_part(sh, d$fix); pw <- lolo_part(sw, d$fix)
  list(name = d$name, group = d$group, H = fh, W = fw, lolo_H = ph, lolo_W = pw, lolo = ph + pw,
       row = stats_row(d$name, d$group, fh$E + fw$E, ph + pw, NA_real_, length(fh$par) + length(fw$par)) |>
         mutate(lambda_H = fh$par[1], lambda_W = fw$par[1]))
}

in_cluster <- function(items, fun) {
  cl <- makeCluster(N_WORKERS)
  on.exit(stopCluster(cl))
  clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})
    source("R/huff.R")
    `%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
  })
  clusterExport(cl, c("dest", "D", "Dn", "dP", "AF", "MH", "MW", "M1", "M3", "DMAX", "FOLDS", "X_VARS", "X_BASE",
                      "idx_old", "idx_new", "mkX", "make_spec", "lolo_part", "stats_row", "score_one", "score_two"),
                envir = globalenv())
  parLapplyLB(cl, items, fun)
}

# ---- The ladder -------------------------------------------------------------------
ladder <- cache_rds("ladder", {
  entries <- list(
    list(kind = "one", name = "M1 Huff, equal A, lambda = -2", group = "Reference", M = M1, vars = character(0), fix = -2),
    list(kind = "one", name = "M2 Huff, equal A, lambda fitted", group = "Reference", M = M1, vars = character(0)),
    list(kind = "one", name = "M3 + LRT and interchange", group = "Reference", M = M1, vars = c("lrt", "ic")),
    list(kind = "one", name = "M4 + bus stops, retail, food", group = "Attraction", M = M1, vars = X_BASE),
    list(kind = "one", name = "M5 + work and dormitory markets", group = "Market", M = M3, vars = X_BASE),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M6 Two purposes", group = "Two purposes", vars = X_BASE, dmax = Inf),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M7 + rail time to the CBD", group = "Two purposes", vars = X_VARS, dmax = Inf),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M8 + 5 km choice set (selected)", group = "Selected", vars = X_VARS, dmax = DMAX),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M8e Exponential decay", group = "Variant", vars = X_VARS, dmax = DMAX, type = "exp"),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M8f lambda = -2 (Zhu et al.)", group = "Variant", vars = X_VARS, dmax = DMAX, fix = -2),
    list(kind = "two", name = "M9 + outside option at the home end", group = "Open model", vars = X_VARS, dmax = DMAX, use_A0 = TRUE)
  )
  out <- in_cluster(entries, function(d) if (d$kind == "one") score_one(d) else score_two(d))
  setNames(out, c("m1", "m2", "m3", "m4", "m5", "m6", "m7", "m8", "m8e", "m8f", "m9"))
})

# M0: everyone uses the nearest station, scaled to total ridership. It has nothing to
# learn beyond that scale, so its hold-out score is its score on the same stations.
nearest_E <- local({
  nn <- apply(D, 1, which.min)
  e <- tapply(M1[, 1], factor(nn, levels = seq_len(ncol(D))), sum)
  e[is.na(e)] <- 0
  as.numeric(e) * sum(dest$daily_in) / sum(e, na.rm = TRUE)
})
row0 <- local({
  E <- pmax(nearest_E, 1); ok <- !is.na(dest$fold); T <- dest$daily_in
  tibble(model = "M0 Nearest station", group = "Reference", lambda = NA_real_, n_par = 1L,
         insample = fit_stats(T, E)$r2_log, insample_rho = fit_stats(T, E)$rho,
         lolo_r2 = fit_stats(T[ok], E[ok])$r2_log, lolo_rmsle = fit_stats(T[ok], E[ok])$rmsle,
         lolo_mape = fit_stats(T[ok], E[ok])$mape, lolo_rho = fit_stats(T[ok], E[ok])$rho)
})

# The transport planner's usual alternative: a direct ridership regression on the same
# variables plus residents within 800 m, with no competition between stations.
drm <- local({
  df <- dest |> mutate(y = log(daily_in))
  fm <- reformulate(c("l_res8", X_VARS), "y")
  pr <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(df))
  for (f in FOLDS) { te <- which(df$fold == f); pr[te] <- predict(lm(fm, df[-te, ]), df[te, ]) }
  m <- lm(fm, df); ok <- !is.na(pr); T <- df$daily_in
  list(model = m, row = tibble(model = "DRM Direct regression", group = "Reference", lambda = NA_real_,
       n_par = length(coef(m)), insample = fit_stats(T, exp(fitted(m)))$r2_log,
       insample_rho = fit_stats(T, exp(fitted(m)))$rho,
       lolo_r2 = fit_stats(T[ok], exp(pr[ok]))$r2_log, lolo_rmsle = fit_stats(T[ok], exp(pr[ok]))$rmsle,
       lolo_mape = fit_stats(T[ok], exp(pr[ok]))$mape, lolo_rho = fit_stats(T[ok], exp(pr[ok]))$rho))
})

ladder_tbl <- bind_rows(row0, drm$row, map_dfr(ladder, "row"))
print(as.data.frame(ladder_tbl |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))

sel  <- ladder$m8
open <- ladder$m9
SP_H <- sel$H$spec; SP_W <- sel$W$spec; SP_O <- open$H$spec
message("selected: lambda H ", round(sel$H$par[1], 3), ", W ", round(sel$W$par[1], 3))

# ---- Fold-level hold-out errors -----------------------------------------------------
fold_tbl <- dest |>
  mutate(pred = sel$lolo, err = log(pred / daily_in)) |>
  filter(!is.na(fold)) |>
  group_by(fold) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_error = median(err), rmsle = sqrt(mean(err^2)),
            actual = sum(daily_in), predicted = sum(pred),
            rho = cor(daily_in, pred, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(total_ratio = predicted / actual)
print(as.data.frame(mutate(fold_tbl, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 2)))))

# Can the model pick out the lowest-ridership stations before they exist? Scored on
# MRT stations held out with their line. AUC is the chance that a station in the
# lowest fifth is ranked below one that is not.
mrt_held <- dest |> mutate(pred = sel$lolo) |> filter(!is.na(fold), lrt == 0)
low_cut  <- quantile(mrt_held$daily_in, 0.2)
auc_low <- local({
  y <- mrt_held$daily_in <= low_cut
  r <- rank(-mrt_held$pred)
  (sum(r[y]) - sum(y) * (sum(y) + 1) / 2) / (sum(y) * sum(!y))
})
hold_bias <- with(mrt_held, median(log(pred / daily_in)))

# ---- Far-field test -----------------------------------------------------------------
# A new station in Jurong should not take riders from Marina Bay. The change at
# stations more than 8 km from any new access point is a plausibility test that the
# hold-out score cannot supply, because a model fits better by letting CBD stations
# draw on residents across the island.
new_xy <- dP[idx_new, c("x", "y")]
km_new <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(dest)), \(i) min(sqrt((dest$x[i] - new_xy$x)^2 + (dest$y[i] - new_xy$y)^2)) / 1000, 0)

pivot_change <- function(fh, sh, fw, sw, X_n = mkX(X_VARS, dP)) {
  bh <- expected(fh$par, sh); nh <- expected(fh$par, sh, D = Dn, X = X_n)
  bw <- expected(fw$par, sw); nw <- expected(fw$par, sw, D = Dn, X = X_n)
  (dest$T_H * nh[idx_old] / pmax(bh, 1e-6) + dest$T_W * nw[idx_old] / pmax(bw, 1e-6)) / dest$daily_in - 1
}

# ---- Profiles -----------------------------------------------------------------------
prof_dmax <- cache_rds("prof_dmax", {
  items <- as.list(c(3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, Inf))
  in_cluster_res <- in_cluster(items, function(dm) {
    sh <- make_spec(dest$T_H, MH, X_VARS, "pow", dm); sw <- make_spec(dest$T_W, MW, X_VARS, "pow", dm)
    fh <- fit_huff(sh); fw <- fit_huff(sw)
    ph <- lolo_part(sh); pw <- lolo_part(sw); p <- ph + pw; ok <- !is.na(p)
    list(dmax = dm, fh = fh, fw = fw, sh = sh, sw = sw,
         insample = fit_stats(dest$daily_in, fh$E + fw$E)$r2_log,
         lolo = fit_stats(dest$daily_in[ok], p[ok])$r2_log, rho = fit_stats(dest$daily_in[ok], p[ok])$rho)
  })
  map_dfr(in_cluster_res, function(z) {
    chg <- pivot_change(z$fh, z$sh, z$fw, z$sw)
    tibble(dmax = z$dmax, lambda_H = z$fh$par[1], lambda_W = z$fw$par[1], insample = z$insample, lolo = z$lolo, rho = z$rho,
           far_median = median(chg[km_new > 8]), far_worst = min(chg[km_new > 8]),
           near_median = median(chg[km_new <= 2]), worst = min(chg))
  })
})
print(as.data.frame(mutate(prof_dmax, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))

prof_lambda <- cache_rds("prof_lambda", {
  grid <- expand.grid(part = c("H", "W"), lambda = c(-0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5, -3, -3.5), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  res <- in_cluster(split(grid, seq_len(nrow(grid))), function(g) {
    sp <- make_spec(if (g$part == "H") dest$T_H else dest$T_W, if (g$part == "H") MH else MW)
    fit <- fit_huff(sp, fix_lambda = g$lambda)
    pred <- lolo_part(sp, g$lambda); ok <- !is.na(pred)
    tibble(part = g$part, lambda = g$lambda, insample = fit_stats(sp$T, fit$E)$r2_log,
           lolo = fit_stats(sp$T[ok], pred[ok])$r2_log)
  })
  bind_rows(res)
})

fit_fixed_A0 <- function(la0, sp, par0) {
  fn <- function(th) loss(c(th, la0), sp)
  gr <- function(th) { g <- grad_loss(c(th, la0), sp); g[-length(g)] }
  o <- optim(par0, fn, gr, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 300, reltol = 1e-8))
  o$par <- c(o$par, la0); o
}
prof_a0 <- cache_rds("prof_a0", {
  grid <- c(-2, -1, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3)
  X <- mkX(X_VARS)
  map_dfr(grid, function(la0) {
    sp <- modifyList(SP_H, list(use_A0 = TRUE))
    o <- fit_fixed_A0(la0, sp, sel$H$par)
    pred <- rep(NA_real_, ncol(D))
    for (f in FOLDS) {
      te <- which(dest$fold == f); tr <- setdiff(seq_len(ncol(D)), te)
      s2 <- modifyList(sp, list(D = D[, tr, drop = FALSE], X = X[tr, , drop = FALSE], T = dest$T_H[tr]))
      o2 <- fit_fixed_A0(la0, s2, sel$H$par)
      pred[te] <- expected(o2$par, s2, D = D, X = X)[te]
    }
    ok <- !is.na(pred)
    z <- model_parts(o$par, sp)
    Xn <- mkX(X_VARS, dP)
    z2 <- model_parts(o$par, sp, D = Dn, X = Xn)
    tibble(lA0 = la0, A0 = exp(la0), lambda = o$par[1], insample = fit_stats(dest$T_H, z$E)$r2_log,
           lolo = fit_stats(dest$T_H[ok], pred[ok])$r2_log,
           share_outside = weighted.mean(1 - rowSums(z$P), z$mk),
           induced = sum(z2$E) - sum(z$E), new_E = sum(z2$E[idx_new]))
  }) |> mutate(share_induced = induced / new_E)
})
print(as.data.frame(mutate(prof_lambda, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))
print(as.data.frame(mutate(prof_a0, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))

# ---- Permutation null -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Is the gain from the attraction variables more than a flexible model would find in
# noise? Bus, retail and food counts are shuffled among stations of the same mode, so
# that the LRT-MRT contrast survives and only their link to ridership is broken.
obs_r2 <- fit_stats(dest$daily_in, sel$H$E + sel$W$E)$r2_log
perm_null <- cache_rds("perm_null", {
  X <- mkX(X_VARS)
  seeds <- 2000 + seq_len(99)
  unlist(in_cluster(as.list(seeds), function(s) {
    set.seed(s)
    Xb <- mkX(X_VARS)
    vv <- c("l_bus", "l_ret", "l_food")
    for (grp in list(which(dest$lrt == 1), which(dest$lrt == 0))) Xb[grp, vv] <- Xb[sample(grp), vv]
    sh <- modifyList(make_spec(dest$T_H, MH), list(X = Xb)); sw <- modifyList(make_spec(dest$T_W, MW), list(X = Xb))
    fit_stats(dest$daily_in, fit_huff(sh)$E + fit_huff(sw)$E)$r2_log
  }))
})
perm_p <- (1 + sum(perm_null >= obs_r2)) / (1 + length(perm_null))
message("permutation: observed ", round(obs_r2, 3), ", null max ", round(max(perm_null), 3), ", p ", perm_p)

# ---- Bootstrap --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A Bayesian bootstrap: stations are reweighted rather than resampled, so every station
# stays in the choice set, as it does in reality, and only its say in the calibration
# varies. The same weights go to both ends in a draw.
boot <- cache_rds("boot", {
  draws <- in_cluster(as.list(seq_len(N_BOOT)), function(b) {
    set.seed(5000 + b)
    w <- rexp(ncol(D)); w <- w / mean(w)
    sh <- modifyList(make_spec(dest$T_H, MH), list(w = w)); sw <- modifyList(make_spec(dest$T_W, MW), list(w = w))
    so <- modifyList(make_spec(dest$T_H, MH, use_A0 = TRUE), list(w = w))
    list(H = fit_huff(sh, maxit = 150)$par, W = fit_huff(sw, maxit = 150)$par, O = fit_huff(so, maxit = 150)$par)
  })
  list(H = do.call(rbind, map(draws, "H")), W = do.call(rbind, map(draws, "W")), O = do.call(rbind, map(draws, "O")))
})

ci_tbl <- function(par, b, names) {
  q <- apply(b, 2, quantile, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(term = names, estimate = par, lo = q[1, ], hi = q[2, ])
}
coef_H <- ci_tbl(sel$H$par, boot$H, c("lambda", X_VARS, paste0("log_kappa_", colnames(MH))))
coef_W <- ci_tbl(sel$W$par, boot$W, c("lambda", X_VARS, paste0("log_kappa_", colnames(MW))))
coef_O <- ci_tbl(open$H$par, boot$O, c("lambda", X_VARS, paste0("log_kappa_", colnames(MH)), "log_A0"))
print(as.data.frame(mutate(coef_H, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))
print(as.data.frame(mutate(coef_W, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))
print(as.data.frame(mutate(coef_O, across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 3)))))

# ---- Exact calibration, for comparison --------------------------------------------------
# What huff.fit() in MCI does: find the attractiveness that reproduces each station's
# ridership exactly, whatever it takes. Its effect on how far a station reaches is what
# persuaded this report to pivot on observed ridership instead.
catch_km <- function(P, DD, mk) as.vector(colSums(mk * P * DD) / pmax(colSums(mk * P), 1e-9))
sh_inf <- ladder$m7$H$spec; fh_inf <- ladder$m7$H
cal_inf <- calibrate_r(fh_inf$par, sh_inf)
cal_tbl <- dest |>
  transmute(destination, station_name, r = cal_inf$r,
            km_structural = catch_km(model_parts(fh_inf$par, sh_inf)$P, D, model_parts(fh_inf$par, sh_inf)$mk),
            km_calibrated = catch_km(model_parts(cal_inf$par, sh_inf, r = cal_inf$r)$P, D,
                                     model_parts(cal_inf$par, sh_inf, r = cal_inf$r)$mk))

# ---- Residual structure ------------------------------------------------------------------
st_pts <- st_as_sf(dest, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3414)
lw <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(st_pts, k = 6)), style = "W")
E_sel <- sel$H$E + sel$W$E
resid_log <- log(dest$daily_in) - log(E_sel)
moran <- moran.mc(resid_log, lw, nsim = 999)
residuals_tbl <- dest |>
  transmute(destination, station_name, x, y, lrt, daily_in, phi, E = E_sel, E_H = sel$H$E, E_W = sel$W$E,
            resid = resid_log, lolo = sel$lolo, fold)

# ---- Against MCI ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# huff.shares() and shares.total() on the interaction frame, using the selected home-end
# model's attractiveness and decay. Both functions need a complete rectangular table, so
# the frame cannot simply be cut at 5 km: a station out of range is moved to a distance so
# great that its share vanishes, and hexagons with no station in range, which send no one
# in the matrix form, are left out.
mci_check <- cache_rds("mci_check", {
  si <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds"))
  q <- unpack(sel$H$par, SP_H)
  att <- tibble(destination = dest$destination, attraction = exp(as.vector(SP_H$X %*% q$beta)))
  mk <- tibble(origin = origins$origin, market = as.vector(SP_H$M %*% q$kappa))
  has <- si |> group_by(origin) |> summarise(any_in = any(distance <= DMAX), .groups = "drop") |> filter(any_in)
  frame <- si |>
    select(origin, destination, distance) |>
    filter(origin %in% has$origin) |>
    mutate(distance = ifelse(distance <= DMAX, distance, 1e9)) |>
    left_join(att, by = "destination") |>
    left_join(mk, by = "origin")
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  sh <- huff.shares(as.data.frame(frame), "origin", "destination", "attraction", "distance",
                    gamma = 1, lambda = q$lambda, atype = "pow", dtype = "pow", check_df = FALSE)
  tot <- shares.total(sh, "origin", "destination", "p_ij", "market", check_df = FALSE)
  secs <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  e <- tot$sum_E_j[match(dest$destination, tot$suppliers_single)]
  list(max_abs_gap = max(abs(e - sel$H$E)), max_rel_gap = max(abs(e / sel$H$E - 1)), seconds = secs, rows = nrow(frame))
})
print(mci_check)

# ---- Fill the attraction column of the frames ---------------------------------------------
attr_of <- function(d, X) tibble(destination = d$destination,
  A_home = exp(as.vector(X %*% unpack(sel$H$par, SP_H)$beta)),
  A_activity = exp(as.vector(X %*% unpack(sel$W$par, SP_W)$beta)))

  left_join(attr_of(dP, mkX(X_VARS, dP)), by = "destination") |> mutate(in_range = distance <= DMAX)
saveRDS(si_e, file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds")); saveRDS(si_p, file.path(DER, "si_proposed.rds"))
